findings.title: Serialize index creation per key before publishing to the cache
findings.body: The narrowed cache lock allows GetIndex to return nil while an index for that same key is being built. Concurrent searches, or a search and the write-event handler, can therefore build separate indexes for one NamespacedResource. If the event handler publishes its index and applies an update before the other builder publishes, the latter replaces the updated index with its older snapshot, losing the update from search results. Disk-backed builds can also compete to create the same directory and fail. Keep builds for different keys parallel, but coordinate creation for the same key and recheck the cache before building.

findings.title: Retain the stopped-state check when removing lazy initialization
findings.body: Removing the Init checks also removes the request guard against shutdown: Stop sets initErr to 'service is stopping' or 'service is stopped', and previously subsequent calls to Init returned that error without executing the operation. Create, Update, Delete and the other RPCs now continue accessing the backend after Stop. For the SQL backend, Stop only cancels polling and does not disable database writes, so requests can successfully mutate resources after the watchers have stopped. Replace the lazy-init checks with an explicit lifecycle-state guard rather than removing the shutdown protection.
